data.narrative:
Pasqal is a pre-IPO quantum computing company that has raised €340M+ to date. The quantum computing sector comprises 9 identifiable peers: 3 public companies (IonQ, Rigetti Computing, D-Wave Quantum) and 6 private competitors including Quantinuum and Infleqtion.

Standard peer-median valuation methodology is not applicable to Pasqal. The quantum computing peer set, while 9 companies strong at the sector level, lacks sufficient depth at comparable stages and valuation tiers. No clustering of same-stage or adjacent-stage peers meeting minimum thresholds (≥3 datapoints) exists. A broad sector-median approach would obscure material differences in technology platform, funding trajectory, and commercial maturity across the fragmented quantum hardware landscape, rendering such a calculation misleading rather than informative.

Without triangulation to a robust peer multiple, valuation of Pasqal requires alternative approaches not present in the supplied data. The primary uncertainties are: (1) absence of recent institutional round pricing or secondary transaction data; (2) heterogeneity in quantum modalities and development timelines across the narrow peer universe; (3) lack of revenue or customer concentration metrics to anchor relative valuation. A credible range would require either a widened comparable universe with normalized financial metrics, or introduction of venture-stage cost-of-capital methodology with explicit assumptions on TAM realization and time-to-exit.
